drhp.business: Gloster Limited manufactures jute goods and allied products and is managed organizationally as a single business. Its integrated operations at Bauria, Howrah, West Bengal span four business units over more than 175 acres, supported by a workforce of more than 4,500 persons, and serve customers in India and outside India across industrial packaging, government procurement and, increasingly, consumer lifestyle markets. Building on this manufacturing base, the Company has embarked on a retail journey through PATSAN, its dedicated consumer brand for sustainable jute lifestyle and home products.

risks.note: Flagged by management as a key concern. The raw jute market witnessed an unprecedented surge in prices during the year, caused by unremunerative prices, adverse weather and lower sowing areas, with prices increasing nearly three-fold on lower crop and reduced carry-over stocks; the steep rise in input costs exerted significant pressure on the jute industry. Even in the ensuing season, prices are expected to remain at elevated levels compared to previous years.
risks.risk: Availability and price of quality raw jute

risks.note: Compulsory packing norms for food grains and sugar stand at 100% and 20% of production respectively, and the notification is valid only up to 30th June 2026. Any dilution of the compulsory Jute Packing Order can adversely affect the market for jute products — a structural demand-base risk since Government demand is a core end market.
risks.risk: Dilution of the compulsory Jute Packing Order (JPMA)

risks.note: Management flags that lower incentives on exports impact competitive pricing in export markets. Exports saw further de-growth during the year largely due to the unprecedented increase in prices of finished goods, apart from the effect of wars affecting all export markets.
risks.risk: Export competitiveness and lower export incentives

risks.note: Management flags the banning of import of specific jute products from Bangladesh via all land routes as a risk/concern, and separately notes export markets already lost to Bangladesh that it hopes to win back only if prices correct.
risks.risk: Competition from Bangladesh and trade-route restrictions

risks.note: BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: jute manufacturing is inherently energy intensive across fibre processing, spinning, weaving and finishing, while jute cultivation is largely rain-fed and highly sensitive to climate variability — erratic monsoons, flooding and rising temperatures can adversely affect raw jute availability, fibre quality and procurement timelines. Regulatory and market expectations to decarbonise add transition risk.

BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: operations generate emissions from boilers, generators and fibre handling including particulate matter and combustion-related emissions. Inadequate control may cause regulatory non-compliance, penalties, operational disruption and reputational damage, heightened by customer focus on environmentally responsible sourcing.

BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: water is a critical input in batching, softening and washing. Inefficient use or improper discharge of untreated effluent with high organic load may cause regulatory non-compliance, environmental degradation and community concerns, especially in water-stressed areas.

BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: land use change, emissions, wastewater discharge and waste disposal can directly or indirectly impact local biodiversity, while jute cultivation itself depends on healthy agro-ecosystems, making biodiversity conservation material to long-term resource security.
